records.label: thm:tensor_quotient
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Completed tensor quotient]\label{thm:tensor_quotient}
Let \(R_1,\ldots,R_s\) be complete Noetherian local \(\OO\) algebras with common residue field \(k\). Let \(I_i\subseteq R_i\) be closed ideals. Put
\[
R^{\mathrm{loc}}=R_1\wideotimes_{\OO}\cdots\wideotimes_{\OO}R_s
\]
and let \(J\) be the closed ideal generated by the images of the \(I_i\). Then there is a canonical isomorphism
\[
\boxed{
(R_1/I_1)\wideotimes_{\OO}\cdots\wideotimes_{\OO}(R_s/I_s)
\cong
R^{\mathrm{loc}}/J.
}
\]
\end{theorem}
records.proof_tex:
Write \(S=\bigotimes_{i=1}^{s}R_i\) for the ordinary tensor product. Its ideal of definition is
\[
\fraka=\frakm_{\OO}S+\sum_i\frakm_{R_i}S,
\qquad L=\sum_i I_iS.
\]
The scalar term retains the base adic topology when the family is empty. The ordinary quotient theorem gives a canonical algebra isomorphism
\[
S/L\cong\bigotimes_{i=1}^{s}(R_i/I_i),
\]
carrying the image of \(\fraka\) to the defining ideal on the right. The quotient topology on \(S/L\) is precisely this image ideal topology.

Here completion means the actual Hausdorff completion for the additive uniformity of the indicated adic topology. For every adic ring \(S\) and ideal \(L\), there is a canonical bicontinuous ring isomorphism
\[
\widehat S\big/\overline{L\widehat S}\cong\widehat{S/L}.
\]
Indeed, the completed quotient map kills the closed extended ideal. In the other direction, the quotient map from \(S/L\) to \(\widehat S/\overline{L\widehat S}\) extends to its completion. The latter quotient is complete: the adic uniformity has a countable base, and the quotient of a complete countably based additive group is complete. Its closed defining subgroup makes it Hausdorff. The two composites agree with the identity on dense quotient representatives, so continuity proves both inverse laws.

Applying this comparison to the displayed ordinary tensor isomorphism proves the claim. The closed extended ideal is exactly \(J\), since extension commutes with the finite sum of the factor ideals. The maps preserve coefficients and each canonical factor map. The common residue field identifies \(S/\fraka\) with \(k\); finite generation of \(\fraka\), supplied by the Noetherian factor hypotheses, identifies the completed topology with its maximal ideal topology. Proper quotients retain locality. If a condition is the unit ideal, the ring comparison remains valid with the zero ring, without treating it as a local ring with residue field \(k\).
records.normalized_claim: Finite complete Noetherian local O-algebras with common residue k and closed I_i: actual completed tensor of quotients equals actual completion modulo closed generated ideal, canonically/bicontinuously.
records.dependencies: Ordinary tensor quotient; completion/closed-quotient comparison; common residue maps
records.decisive_obligation: Actual topology, closed relation ideal, coefficient/factor maps, inverse laws, empty/unary/unit cases

records.label: cor:simultaneous_local
records.proof_tex: Let \(f:R^{\mathrm{loc}}\to A\) be the point. Since \(A\) is Hausdorff and \(f\) is continuous, \(\ker f\) is closed. Thus it contains the closed ideal \(J\) if and only if it contains the algebraic ideal generated by the images of the \(I_i\). This is equivalent to every local restriction killing \(I_i\). The universal property of the actual ideal quotient gives the factors, and the quotient topology gives their continuity. Surjectivity of the quotient map gives uniqueness. If \(f\) reflects units, lift an element of the quotient to the original ring to see that its factor also reflects units.
records.normalized_claim: Every continuous Hausdorff-target point factors uniquely/continuously through the closed local-condition quotient iff all factor restrictions kill I_i; local factors when original point local.
records.decisive_obligation: Closed kernel contains closure exactly when it contains factor relations; uniqueness/locality

records.label: prop:global_local_basechange
records.proof_tex:
Put \(A=R^{\mathrm{loc}}\), \(B=R^\square\), and let \(J\subseteq A\) be the closed local condition ideal. By \cref{thm:tensor_quotient}, the independently constructed ring \(R^{\mathrm{loc},\tau}\) is canonically \(A/J\). The ordinary tensor identity
\[
B\otimes_A(A/J)\cong B/JB
\]
carries the defining ideal of the tensor to the image of \(\frakm_B\). Here the structural map is local by the stated global deformation datum, so it carries \(\frakm_A\) into \(\frakm_B\). Completing, and applying the completion and quotient comparison from the preceding proof, gives a bicontinuous isomorphism
\[
R^\tau\cong B/\overline{JB}.
\]
The construction commutes with the canonical map from \(B\), which is therefore surjective. It is also unchanged by transporting the tensor factor from \(A/J\) to the actual completed tensor of the local quotients. The transported ideal is exactly its natural defining ideal.

For a continuous algebra point \(x:B\to C\) with complete Hausdorff target, the kernel of \(x\) is closed. Consequently \(x\) has a unique continuous factor through \(R^\tau\) if and only if it kills \(JB\), equivalently if its restriction to \(A\) kills \(J\). By \cref{cor:simultaneous_local}, this is exactly the requirement that all local restrictions satisfy their quotient conditions. The factor is an algebra map because its composite with the canonical global map is \(x\). If \(x\) is local, surjectivity of that map shows that its factor reflects units and is local. Uniqueness also proves naturality under coefficient preserving maps of targets. This identifies the represented base change; it does not supply representability of a new arithmetic deformation problem.
records.normalized_claim: Supplied complete Noetherian local deformation rings and continuous local O-map: actual completed global base change represents simultaneous local quotient conditions on continuous local O-test points.
records.decisive_obligation: Tensor ideal transported to m_B; actual completed global object; coefficient/naturality/locality contract

records.label: prop:local_idempotent
records.proof_tex: Let \(e^2=e\). Since \(e+(1-e)=1\), at least one of \(e\) and \(1-e\) is a unit. If \(e\) is a unit, then \(e=1\). If \(1-e\) is a unit, then \(e=0\).
records.normalized_claim: Every idempotent in a commutative local ring is zero or one.
records.decisive_obligation: One of e,1-e is a unit; cancellation

records.label: thm:s3_adequacy
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Finite adequacy certificate]\label{thm:s3_adequacy}
The standard representation of \(S_3\) over \(\FF_7\) is adequate. More precisely,
\[
H^0(S_3,\ad^0V)=0,
\qquad
H^1(S_3,\FF_7)=0,
\qquad
H^1(S_3,\ad^0V)=0,
\]
and
\[
\ad^0V\cong\operatorname{sgn}\oplus V.
\]
The sign summand is detected by an eigenprojector of a three cycle, and the standard summand is detected by an eigenprojector of a transposition.
\end{theorem}
records.proof_tex:
The coordinate map
\[
(a,b)\longmapsto(a,-a+b,-b)
\]
identifies the displayed matrices with the permutation action on the sum zero subspace of \(\FF_7^3\). This action is faithful. The four matrices \(1,s,t,st\) span \(M_2\) over every field of characteristic seven: the determinant of their coordinate matrix is \(4\ne0\). A subspace stable under the group is therefore stable under every endomorphism, so the representation is absolutely irreducible. The characteristic polynomials of the identity, transpositions, and three cycles are respectively
\[
(X-1)^2,\qquad (X-1)(X+1),\qquad (X-2)(X-4).
\]
Thus all eigenvalues already lie in \(\FF_7\).

A trace zero matrix fixed by conjugation by both \(s\) and \(t\) is zero, as follows by comparing its four entries. This proves \(H^0(S_3,\ad^0V)=0\). For any \(\FF_7[S_3]\) module \(M\) and one cocycle \(f\), put
\[
u=-6^{-1}\sum_{h\in S_3}f(h).
\]
Summing \(f(gh)=g f(h)+f(g)\) over \(h\) gives \(gu-u=f(g)\). Hence every one cocycle is a coboundary and \(H^1(S_3,M)=0\), giving both asserted first cohomology vanishings.

Write
\[
W(a,b,c)=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&-a\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
Z=W(2,3,4),\quad A=W(1,1,2),\quad B=W(1,5,6).
\]
The three coordinate columns have determinant \(3\ne0\). Under conjugation,
\[
sZ=-Z,\quad tZ=Z,\qquad
sA=-A,\quad sB=A+B,\quad tA=B,\quad tB=-A-B.
\]
Consequently \((z,(a,b))\mapsto zZ+aA+bB\) is an equivariant isomorphism from \(\operatorname{sgn}\oplus V\) to \(\ad^0V\).

The sign witness is \(W_{\mathrm{sgn}}=Z\), while
\(W_{\mathrm{std}}=W(6,4,3)=3A+3B\) belongs to the standard summand. The corresponding projectors and trace pairings are
\[
P_{t,2}=\begin{pmatrix}2&4\\3&6\end{pmatrix},
\qquad \Tr(P_{t,2}W_{\mathrm{sgn}})=3\ne0,
\]
\[
P_{s,1}=\begin{pmatrix}0&4\\0&1\end{pmatrix},
\qquad \Tr(P_{s,1}W_{\mathrm{std}})=6\ne0.
\]
For an operator \(D\) with \((D-\alpha I)(D-\beta I)=0\) and \(\alpha\ne\beta\), the canonical projector is
\[
P_{D,\alpha}=(\alpha-\beta)^{-1}(D-\beta I).
\]
Its image equals \(\ker((D-\alpha I)^n)\) for every \(n\ge1\), and it kills \(\ker((D-\beta I)^n)\). This identifies the displayed matrices with the generalized eigenspace projectors required in the adequacy definition.

For detection on every irreducible submodule, one can check the stronger assertion that canonical projectors detect every nonzero matrix. In addition to the two projectors above, use
\[
P_{s,-1}=\begin{pmatrix}1&3\\0&0\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
P_{tst^{-1},1}=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\4&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The four trace pairings with these matrices have trivial common kernel in \(M_2(\FF_7)\), by row reduction. Every irreducible adjoint submodule contains a nonzero matrix, so some canonical projector has nonzero trace pairing on that submodule. This verifies the last adequacy clause and completes the certificate.
records.normalized_claim: The actual faithful standard S3 representation over F7 is absolutely irreducible and adequate with specified adjoint splitting, H0/H1 vanishings and projector witnesses.
records.dependencies: Declared adequacy definition; displayed permutation and adjoint actions
records.decisive_obligation: Actual representation/domain, averaging, absolute irreducibility, every adjoint constituent detected

records.label: prop:group_algebra_transfer
records.statement_tex:
\begin{proposition}[Functorial group algebra transfer]\label{prop:group_algebra_transfer}
A group homomorphism \(q:\Delta'\to\Delta\) induces an \(\OO\) algebra homomorphism
\[
q_*:\OO[\Delta']\longrightarrow\OO[\Delta].
\]
If \(q\) is surjective, then \(q_*\) is surjective. Augmentation commutes with the transfer:
\[
\epsilon_\Delta q_*=\epsilon_{\Delta'}.
\]
\end{proposition}
records.proof_tex: Extend \(q\) linearly from the group basis. Multiplicativity follows from \(q(gh)=q(g)q(h)\). Surjectivity follows because every basis element of \(\OO[\Delta]\) has a preimage. Both augmentation maps send every group element to one, which gives the final identity.
records.normalized_claim: Every group map induces coefficient group-algebra map; surjectivity preserved; augmentations commute.
records.decisive_obligation: Multiplicativity, coefficient preservation, arbitrary groups

records.label: thm:residual_augmentation_algebra
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Residual augmentation algebra]\label{thm:residual_augmentation_algebra}
Suppose
\[
\Delta\cong
\prod_{i=1}^{r}C_{p^{n_i}}.
\]
Choose generators \(\gamma_i\), and let \(X_i=\gamma_i-1\). Then
\[
\boxed{
k[\Delta]
\cong
k[X_1,\ldots,X_r]
\big/
(X_1^{p^{n_1}},\ldots,X_r^{p^{n_r}}).
}
\]
The augmentation ideal is generated by the \(X_i\), and \(k[\Delta]\) is local.
\end{theorem}
records.proof_tex:
In characteristic \(p\),
\[
(1+X_i)^{p^{n_i}}-1=X_i^{p^{n_i}}.
\]
Thus the assignment \(X_i\mapsto\gamma_i-1\) gives a surjective homomorphism from the displayed truncated polynomial ring to \(k[\Delta]\). Both sides have dimension \(\prod_ip^{n_i}=\abs{\Delta}\) over \(k\), so the map is an isomorphism. The quotient by the ideal generated by the \(X_i\) is \(k\). Since each \(X_i\) is nilpotent, that ideal is the unique maximal ideal.
records.normalized_claim: For finite abelian p-group product of cyclic p-powers, residual algebra is the actual multivariate monomial quotient, local with declared augmentation generators.
records.dependencies: Characteristic p binomial law; group basis
records.decisive_obligation: Algebra isomorphism and dimension; r=0 or trivial cyclic factors

records.label: cor:no_residual_character_splitting
records.proof_tex:
The first assertion follows from locality in \cref{thm:residual_augmentation_algebra}. For the general finite \(p\) group assertion, let \(e\in k[G]\) be idempotent and write \(\epsilon:k[G]\to k\) for augmentation. Suppose \(\epsilon(e)=0\) and \(e\ne0\). The \(\FF_p\) span \(W\) of the left translates \(ge\) is a nonzero finite dimensional \(\FF_p\) vector space, stable under \(G\). Its cardinality is divisible by \(p\). The orbit counting formula implies that its fixed point set also has cardinality divisible by \(p\). Since zero is fixed, there is a nonzero fixed vector \(v\in W\).

A vector in the regular representation fixed by all left translations has constant coefficients. Consequently \(ve=\epsilon(e)v=0\). On the other hand, \(e^2=e\) implies \(we=w\) for every \(w\in W\), hence \(ve=v\), a contradiction. Thus every idempotent of augmentation zero is zero. Since \(\epsilon(e)^2=\epsilon(e)\) in the field \(k\), either \(\epsilon(e)=0\) or \(\epsilon(e)=1\); in the latter case apply the preceding argument to \(1-e\).
records.normalized_claim: Every finite p-group over every characteristic-p field has no nontrivial residual group-algebra idempotents, including nonabelian groups.
records.dependencies: Finite prime-field orbit span; orbit counting;5.2 abelian case
records.decisive_obligation: Nonzero fixed vector; regular action and right multiplication; no finite-field restriction on k

records.label: thm:coinvariant_recovery
records.proof_tex: Choose a \(\Lambda\) basis of \(M\). Tensoring the resulting isomorphism \(M\cong\Lambda^d\) along augmentation gives \(\OO^d\). Tensoring by \(\Lambda/\fraka\) is the same as quotienting by \(\fraka M\).
records.normalized_claim: A free rank-d right auxiliary group-algebra module has coinvariant/tensor recovery O^d; all coefficient primes.
records.decisive_obligation: Right/left convention, basis transport, rank zero

records.label: thm:finite_module_support
records.proof_tex:
Let \(\frakp\in\Spec R\). If \(\Ann_R(M)\not\subseteq\frakp\), choose
\(a\in\Ann_R(M)\setminus\frakp\). The element \(a\) becomes a unit in
\(R_{\frakp}\), so \(M_{\frakp}=0\).

Conversely, suppose \(M_{\frakp}=0\). Choose generators
\(m_1,\ldots,m_d\) of \(M\). For each \(i\), there is an element
\(s_i\notin\frakp\) such that \(s_im_i=0\). The product
\(s=s_1\cdots s_d\) lies outside \(\frakp\) and annihilates every generator.
Thus \(s\in\Ann_R(M)\setminus\frakp\). This proves the equality.
records.normalized_claim: Every finite module over any commutative ring has support V(annihilator).
records.decisive_obligation: Product of annihilating denominators stays outside prime

records.label: thm:fitting_support
records.proof_tex:
If \(M=0\), the statement follows from the usual convention \(\Fitt_0(0)=R\). Assume \(M\neq0\), and choose a finite presentation
\[
R^m\xrightarrow{A}R^n\longrightarrow M\longrightarrow0
\]
with \(n\geq1\).
The zeroth Fitting ideal is generated by the \(n\) by \(n\) minors of \(A\). After localization at a prime \(\frakp\), the module \(M_{\frakp}\) vanishes exactly when \(A_{\frakp}\) is surjective. A map onto the free module \(R_{\frakp}^n\) is surjective exactly when one maximal minor is a unit. Thus \(M_{\frakp}=0\) exactly when \(\Fitt_0^R(M)\not\subseteq\frakp\).
records.normalized_claim: Finite module over Noetherian ring has support V(Fitt_0).
records.decisive_obligation: Local surjectivity iff maximal minor unit; M=0 convention

records.label: thm:higher_fitting_strata
records.proof_tex:
Use a finite presentation with target rank \(n\). If \(r>n\), every fiber has dimension at most \(n\), so the left hand locus is empty. The convention \(\Fitt_{r-1}(M)=R\) for \(r-1\geq n\) makes the right hand locus empty as well. It remains to consider \(1\leq r\leq n\). At \(\frakp\), the fiber dimension is
\[
n-\rank A(\frakp).
\]
It is at least \(r\) exactly when the rank is at most \(n-r\), which is equivalent to the vanishing of every minor of size \(n-r+1\). Those minors generate \(\Fitt_{r-1}^R(M)\).
records.normalized_claim: Finite Noetherian module: fiber-generator dimension at least r iff Fitt_(r-1) vanishes, every r>=1.
records.decisive_obligation: Large-index r>n and n=0 boundary; minors for 1<=r<=n

records.label: prop:fitting_base_change
records.proof_tex: Base change carries a finite presentation matrix for \(M\) to a presentation matrix for \(M\otimes_RS\). Every defining minor is carried to the corresponding minor over \(S\).
records.normalized_claim: Every higher Fitting ideal of a finitely presented module commutes with arbitrary coefficient base change.
records.dependencies: Finite presentation minors; intrinsic Fitting ideals
records.decisive_obligation: Nonflat base change allowed; presentation still right-exact

records.label: thm:near_faithful_full_support
records.proof_tex:
By \cref{thm:finite_module_support}, full support is equivalent to
\[
V\bigl(\Ann_R(M)\bigr)=\Spec R.
\]
This holds exactly when \(\Ann_R(M)\) is contained in every prime ideal, hence in the nilradical. Because \(R\) is Noetherian, the ideal \(\Ann_R(M)\) is finitely generated. An ideal generated by finitely many nilpotent elements is nilpotent. This proves the equivalence of the first three conditions. If \(R\) is reduced, its nilradical is zero.
records.normalized_claim: Finite module over Noetherian ring: nilpotent annihilator iff full support iff annihilator in nilradical; reduced ring gives faithfulness.
records.decisive_obligation: Ideal generated by finitely many nilpotents is nilpotent

records.label: cor:every_component_support
records.proof_tex: Every generic point is a prime of \(R\), and full support contains every prime.
records.normalized_claim: Every generic component point lies in the support of a nearly faithful finite Noetherian module.
records.decisive_obligation: Correct component/generic-point quantifier

records.label: thm:quotient_support
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Support after a quotient]\label{thm:quotient_support}
Let \(R\) be Noetherian, let \(I\subseteq R\) be an ideal, and let \(M\) be a finite \(R\) module. Under the canonical identification
\[
\Spec(R/I)\cong V(I)\subseteq\Spec R,
\]
one has
\[
\boxed{
\Supp_{R/I}(M/IM)
=
\Supp_R(M)\cap V(I).
}
\]
\end{theorem}
records.proof_tex:
Let \(\frakp\supseteq I\). Localizing gives
\[
(M/IM)_{\frakp}
\cong
M_{\frakp}/I_{\frakp}M_{\frakp}.
\]
If \(M_{\frakp}=0\), the quotient is zero. If \(M_{\frakp}\neq0\), then
\(I_{\frakp}\) lies in the maximal ideal of the local ring \(R_{\frakp}\). Nakayama's lemma shows that
\(M_{\frakp}/I_{\frakp}M_{\frakp}\neq0\). The stated equality follows.
records.normalized_claim: Finite Noetherian module specialized to R/I has support Supp(M) intersect V(I), including I=R.
records.decisive_obligation: Finite nonzero M_p remains nonzero modulo I_p in maximal ideal

records.label: thm:ordinary_support_descent
records.proof_tex:
Apply \cref{thm:quotient_support} with \(I=\fraka\). The support of the quotient is
\[
\Spec R_\infty\cap V(\fraka)=V(\fraka),
\]
which identifies with \(\Spec R\). The remaining statements follow from
\cref{thm:near_faithful_full_support}.
records.normalized_claim: Actual ordinary patched quotient/control datum with full patched support gives full finite-level support and near faithfulness; reduced quotient faithful.
records.decisive_obligation: Full support supplied only at patched level; finite/control hypotheses

records.label: cor:componentwise_occupancy
records.proof_tex: The module \(M\) has full support by \cref{thm:ordinary_support_descent}.
records.normalized_claim: Each finite-level irreducible component is contained in full supported locus under ordinary descent.
records.decisive_obligation: Corrected containment direction

records.label: thm:derived_quotient_support
records.proof_tex:
Choose a bounded complex \(P\) of finite projective \(R\) modules representing \(C\). Scalar extension to a commutative \(R\) algebra \(S\) is computed degree by degree as \(S\otimes_RP\); the canonical symmetry of tensor products gives the displayed order \(C\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S\). Scalar extension preserves the bounds, finite generation, and projectivity of the terms. A derived isomorphism between two such projective models lifts to a homotopy equivalence, which scalar extension preserves. The resulting derived object and its residue field fibers are therefore independent of the chosen model.

Let \(q\in\Spec(R/I)\), and let \(\frakp\) be its inverse image in \(R\). The composite point \(R\to R/I\to\kappa(q)\) has kernel \(\frakp\), so it factors through a field embedding \(\kappa(\frakp)\to\kappa(q)\). The ordinary tensor associator in every degree gives an isomorphism of complexes
\[
\kappa(q)\otimes_{R/I}\bigl((R/I)\otimes_RP\bigr)
\cong\kappa(q)\otimes_RP
\cong\kappa(q)\otimes_{\kappa(\frakp)}
\bigl(\kappa(\frakp)\otimes_RP\bigr).
\]
Extension of fields is faithfully flat. It preserves and reflects exactness in each degree, hence also acyclicity. The left hand complex is thus nonzero in the derived category exactly when the residue field fiber of \(C\) at \(\frakp\) is nonzero. This proves the support identity on corresponding primes. The image of \(\Spec(R/I)\to\Spec R\) is exactly \(V(I)\), giving the stated ambient spectrum equality, including the case \(I=R\).
records.normalized_claim: Every perfect complex over a commutative ring has quotient derived support equal to original support intersect V(I).
records.dependencies: Bounded finite-projective model; tensor associativity; faithful field extension
records.decisive_obligation: Actual derived fibers; model independence; quotient spectrum; I=R

records.label: thm:derived_support_descent
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Derived patching support descent]\label{thm:derived_support_descent}
Let \((R_\infty,\fraka,C_\infty,R,C)\) be a derived patching datum. If
\[
\Supp_{R_\infty}(C_\infty)=\Spec R_\infty,
\]
then
\[
\boxed{
\Supp_R(C)=\Spec R.
}
\]
For every point \(x:R\to E'\) to a field, the derived fiber
\[
C\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}\limits_{R,x}^{\mathbf L}}E'
\]
is nonzero.
\end{theorem}
records.proof_tex:
Apply \cref{thm:derived_quotient_support} to the patched complex and use the actual ring identification \(R\cong R_\infty/\fraka\). Full patched support restricts to \(V(\fraka)\), which corresponds to all of \(\Spec R\). The supplied derived isomorphism with \(C\) preserves this support by the projective model argument in that theorem.

For a field valued point \(x:R\to E'\), put \(\frakp=\ker x\). The point factors as \(R\to\kappa(\frakp)\to E'\), where the second map is a field embedding. Tensor association on a projective model identifies the fiber at \(x\) with the extension to \(E'\) of the fiber at \(\frakp\). The latter is nonzero by full support. Faithful flatness of the field extension reflects exactness in every degree, so the fiber at \(x\) is nonzero as well. This applies to every field valued point, with no closed point restriction.
records.normalized_claim: Full patched derived support and actual derived control imply full finite-level derived support and nonzero fiber at every field point.
records.decisive_obligation: Kernel residue field factorization and faithful extension for any field point

records.label: cor:derived_degree_survives
records.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[A nonzero cohomological degree survives]\label{cor:derived_degree_survives}
Under the hypotheses of \cref{thm:derived_support_descent}, for every field valued point \(x:R\to E'\), there is an integer \(i\) such that
\[
H^i
\left(
C\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}\limits_{R,x}^{\mathbf L}}E'
\right)
\neq0.
\]
\end{corollary}
records.proof_tex: The derived fiber is nonzero by \cref{thm:derived_support_descent}. If every cohomology object vanished, a cochain model of that fiber would be acyclic. Its image in the derived category would then be zero, a contradiction. Hence some integer degree has nonzero cohomology.
records.normalized_claim: Every such nonzero derived field fiber has some nonzero integer cohomology degree.
records.decisive_obligation: Cohomology not confused with a nonzero complex term

records.label: thm:rt_support_transport
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Support and Fitting transport]\label{thm:rt_support_transport}
Let \(\varphi:R\to\TT\) be an isomorphism of Noetherian rings. Let \(M\) be a finite \(\TT\) module, viewed as an \(R\) module through \(\varphi\). Then the homeomorphism
\[
\varphi^*:\Spec\TT\longrightarrow\Spec R
\]
satisfies
\[
\boxed{
\varphi^*\bigl(\Supp_{\TT}(M)\bigr)
=
\Supp_R(M).
}
\]
For every \(j\geq0\),
\[
\boxed{
\varphi
\left(
\Fitt_j^R(M)
\right)
=
\Fitt_j^{\TT}(M).
}
\]
\end{theorem}
records.proof_tex: Localization commutes with transport along an isomorphism, so a localization of \(M\) vanishes on one side exactly when the corresponding localization vanishes on the other. This proves the support identity. A finite presentation matrix over \(R\) is carried entry by entry to a presentation matrix over \(\TT\). The minors generating each Fitting ideal are therefore carried to the corresponding minors.
records.normalized_claim: Ring isomorphism of Noetherian R,T and finite T-module transports support and all intrinsic Fitting ideals.
records.decisive_obligation: Actual spectrum homeomorphism and module action

records.label: cor:rt_full_support
records.proof_tex: Apply the support homeomorphism in \cref{thm:rt_support_transport}.
records.normalized_claim: Full support of the same finite module is invariant under actual R=T isomorphism.
records.decisive_obligation: Support carried by full homeomorphism

records.label: prop:quotient_erases_component
records.statement_tex:
\begin{proposition}[A quotient can erase a component]\label{prop:quotient_erases_component}
Let
\[
R=k[[x,y]]/(xy)
\]
and let
\[
\TT=R/(x)\cong k[[y]].
\]
Viewed as an \(R\) module, \(\TT\) has support \(V(x)\), which misses the generic point \((y)\) of the other irreducible component. Thus a surjection \(R\twoheadrightarrow\TT\) does not by itself imply full component occupancy.
\end{proposition}
records.proof_tex: The annihilator of the \(R\) module \(\TT\) is \((x)\). Hence its support is \(V(x)\) by \cref{thm:finite_module_support}. The prime \((y)\) does not contain \(x\), so it is not in this support.
records.normalized_claim: Node quotient R=k[[x,y]]/(xy) to R/(x)=k[[y]] misses generic point (y).
records.decisive_obligation: Actual two components; annihilator (x); generic point exclusion

records.label: thm:field_fiber_criterion
records.proof_tex:
The map \(x\) factors through the local ring \(R_{\frakp}\) and then through an embedding of the residue field \(\kappa(\frakp)\) into \(E'\). Since \(M\) is finite, Nakayama's lemma gives
\[
M_{\frakp}\neq0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
M\otimes_R\kappa(\frakp)\neq0.
\]
Extension of scalars from \(\kappa(\frakp)\) to \(E'\) preserves nonzero vector spaces.
records.normalized_claim: Finite module at any field point x has nonzero actual tensor fiber iff kernel x is in support.
records.decisive_obligation: Finite generation essential; generic/nonclosed point allowed

records.label: cor:supported_hecke_fiber
records.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Supported deformation points give nonzero Hecke fibers]\label{cor:supported_hecke_fiber}
Let \(R\cong\TT\), and let \(M\) be a finite Hecke module. If a point
\(x:R\to E'\) lies in \(\Supp_R(M)\), then the corresponding Hecke fiber
\[
M\otimes_{\TT,x}E'
\]
is nonzero.
\end{corollary}
records.proof_tex:
Transport the support through \cref{thm:rt_support_transport}, then apply
\cref{thm:field_fiber_criterion}.
records.normalized_claim: Supported deformation point under actual R=T and finite Hecke module has nonzero Hecke fiber.
records.decisive_obligation: Compatible transported character

records.label: thm:canonical_hecke_packets
records.proof_tex: The idempotent relations in \cref{fact:artin_decomposition} give the direct sum decomposition. Localization at \(\frakm\) kills every factor except the \(\frakm\) factor, where \(e_{\frakm}\) becomes one. Thus the localization map identifies \(e_{\frakm}V\) with \(V_{\frakm}\). The final statement is the definition of support.
records.normalized_claim: Finite commutative Hecke algebra and finite module decompose by canonical Artin idempotents; packet equals actual localization and detects support.
records.decisive_obligation: Canonical localization maps; orthogonal-idempotent direct sum

records.label: cor:simultaneous_generalized_eigenspaces
records.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Simultaneous generalized eigenspaces]\label{cor:simultaneous_generalized_eigenspaces}
Assume that \(E'\) is algebraically closed and that \(\TT\) is generated by commuting operators \(T_1,\ldots,T_d\) on \(V\). For a maximal ideal
\[
\frakm
=
(T_1-\lambda_1,\ldots,T_d-\lambda_d),
\]
there is an integer \(N\geq1\) such that
\[
\boxed{
e_{\frakm}V
=
\left\{
v\in V:
(T_i-\lambda_i)^Nv=0
\text{ for every }i
\right\}.
}
\]
Thus the canonical Artin packet is the simultaneous generalized eigenspace.
\end{corollary}
records.proof_tex:
The maximal ideal of the Artin local algebra \(\TT_{\frakm}\) is nilpotent. Hence a common power of every \(T_i-\lambda_i\) kills the local packet. On every other local factor, at least one \(T_i-\lambda_i\) is a unit, so no nonzero vector can satisfy all the displayed nilpotence conditions.

Conversely, suppose every \((T_i-\lambda_i)^N\) kills \(v\). Every monomial of total degree greater than \(d(N-1)\) contains one factor to exponent at least \(N\). Therefore a power of \(\frakm\) kills \(v\), which places \(v\) in the \(\frakm\) primary packet.
records.normalized_claim: Over algebraically closed field, canonical packet of a finite commuting generating list is one simultaneous generalized eigenspace with uniform positive exponent.
records.decisive_obligation: Generator/eigenvalue convention, common exponent, nonsemisimple action

records.label: cor:rank_trace_detection
records.proof_tex: An idempotent linear map has minimal polynomial dividing \(X(X-1)\), which has distinct roots. It is diagonalizable with eigenvalues zero and one. Its trace and rank both equal the multiplicity of the eigenvalue one. A positive integer is nonzero in characteristic zero.
records.normalized_claim: Characteristic-zero idempotent projector trace equals dimension cast; occupancy iff positive rank iff nonzero trace.
records.decisive_obligation: Coefficient cast; characteristic-zero restriction essential

records.label: thm:nested_finite_carrier
records.proof_tex:
The displayed relations give
\[
e_{m+1}V\subseteq e_mV.
\]
The nonnegative dimensions form a nonincreasing sequence of positive integers, so they eventually become constant. Once two consecutive dimensions agree, the corresponding inclusion is equality. Thus the ranges stabilize at a nonzero subspace, which is their intersection.
records.normalized_claim: Nonzero nested idempotent ranges in one finite-dimensional carrier stabilize with nonzero intersection.
records.decisive_obligation: No inference for infinite carrier

records.label: cor:finite_witness_incompatibility
records.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Finite witness of incompatibility]\label{cor:finite_witness_incompatibility}
Under the hypotheses of \cref{thm:nested_finite_carrier}, if
\[
\bigcap_{m\geq1}e_mV=0,
\]
then \(e_mV=0\) for some finite \(m\).
\end{corollary}
records.proof_tex: This is the contrapositive of \cref{thm:nested_finite_carrier}.
records.normalized_claim: In the same finite carrier, zero intersection has finite empty packet witness.
records.decisive_obligation: Same finite carrier retained

records.label: lem:stable_core_surjectivity
records.proof_tex:
Fix \(y\in Y_m\). For \(n\geq m+1\), let
\[
A_n
=
\left\{
z\in\im(f_{n,m+1}):
f_{m+1,m}(z)=y
\right\}.
\]
Each \(A_n\) is a nonempty affine subspace of \(V_{m+1}\), and the sequence
\((A_n)\) is descending. A descending sequence of affine subspaces in a finite dimensional vector space stabilizes whenever every term is nonempty. Choose an element in its stable value. It lies in \(Y_{m+1}\) and maps to \(y\).
records.normalized_claim: Every transition of a coherent finite-dimensional vector inverse system surjects on stable cores.
records.decisive_obligation: Actual coherent images and all preimage constraints

records.label: thm:nonzero_stable_core
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Nonzero stable core criterion]\label{thm:nonzero_stable_core}
Let \((V_m)\) be an inverse system of finite dimensional vector spaces. If
\[
Y_m\neq0
\]
for every \(m\), then
\[
\boxed{
\varprojlim_mV_m
\neq0.
}
\]
More precisely, the inverse limit contains a compatible sequence whose first coordinate is any prescribed nonzero element of \(Y_1\).
\end{theorem}
records.proof_tex:
Choose \(0\neq y_1\in Y_1\). By \cref{lem:stable_core_surjectivity}, choose recursively
\(y_{m+1}\in Y_{m+1}\) mapping to \(y_m\). Every \(y_m\) is nonzero because it maps to the nonzero vector \(y_1\). The sequence \((y_m)\) is a nonzero element of the inverse limit.
records.normalized_claim: Nonzero stable cores give a nonzero actual inverse-limit sequence with any prescribed nonzero first stable vector.
records.decisive_obligation: Strict compatibility and nonzero first coordinate

records.label: cor:surjective_inverse_system
records.proof_tex: Surjectivity gives \(Y_m=V_m\). Apply \cref{thm:nonzero_stable_core}.
records.normalized_claim: Surjective transitions of nonzero finite-dimensional carriers give nonzero inverse limit.
records.decisive_obligation: Nonzero and surjectivity, not level occupancy alone

records.label: thm:support_gives_hecke_system
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Support gives a Hecke eigensystem]\label{thm:support_gives_hecke_system}
Let \(R\cong\TT\), let \(H\) be a finite \(\TT\) module, and let
\(x:R\to E'\) be a field valued point. If
\[
\ker x\in\Supp_R(H),
\]
then
\[
\boxed{
H_x:=H\otimes_{\TT,x}E'\neq0.
}
\]
Every element of \(\TT\) acts on \(H_x\) through the scalar prescribed by \(x\).
\end{theorem}
records.proof_tex:
Nonvanishing follows from \cref{cor:supported_hecke_fiber}. The tensor product relation
\[
th\otimes1=h\otimes x(t)
\]
shows that \(t\in\TT\) acts through \(x(t)\).
records.normalized_claim: Supported finite Hecke carrier under R=T gives actual nonzero scalar fiber with every Hecke element acting through x.
records.decisive_obligation: Actual vector in specialized fiber

records.label: thm:pointwise_galois_realization
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Pointwise Galois realization]\label{thm:pointwise_galois_realization}
Let \(E'\) be a Hausdorff topological field of characteristic zero, with continuous ring operations. Require both \(\rho_x=x\circ\rho_R\) and the attached representation below to be continuous. Assume the following data.
\begin{enumerate}
\item A represented deformation ring \(R\) with universal representation
\[
\rho_R:G_{F,S}\longrightarrow\GL_n(R).
\]
\item An isomorphism \(R\cong\TT\).
\item An automorphic Hecke datum \((\TT,H,(P_v))\).
\item A characteristic zero point \(x:R\to E'\) lying in \(\Supp_R(H)\).
\item A classical automorphic representation \(\pi_x\) occurring in the fiber \(H_x\), together with a semisimple attached representation
\[
\rho_{\pi_x}:G_{F,S}\longrightarrow\GL_n(E')
\]
whose unramified characteristic polynomial is \(x(P_v(X))\).
\item Equality
\[
\det\left(X-\rho_x(\Frob_v)\right)=x(P_v(X))
\]
for \(\rho_x=x\circ\rho_R\) at every unramified place in a Chebotarev dense set.
\end{enumerate}
Then
\[
\boxed{
\rho_x^{\mathrm{ss}}
\cong
\rho_{\pi_x}.
}
\]
If \(\rho_x\) is irreducible, then \(\rho_x\cong\rho_{\pi_x}\).
\end{theorem}
records.proof_tex: The coefficients of the characteristic polynomials of \(\rho_x\) and \(\rho_{\pi_x}\) are continuous and constant on conjugacy classes. Their equality on the declared dense union of Frobenius conjugacy classes therefore extends to every element of \(G_{F,S}\), by Hausdorffness. A semisimplification has the same characteristic polynomials as the original representation. The algebraic Brauer Nesbitt input in \cref{fact:chebotarev_brauer_nesbitt} thus gives \(\rho_x^{\mathrm{ss}}\cong\rho_{\pi_x}\). If \(\rho_x\) is irreducible, it is already semisimple.
records.normalized_claim: Continuous specialization and attached semisimple representation over Hausdorff char-zero field with same dense Frobenius polynomials are isomorphic after semisimplification; irreducible specialization directly.
records.decisive_obligation: Same polynomials and normalization; equality extends by Hausdorff continuity; intertwiner over E'

records.label: cor:full_support_pointwise_automorphy
records.statement_tex:
\begin{corollary}[Full support gives pointwise automorphy on the realized locus]\label{cor:full_support_pointwise_automorphy}
In the setting of \cref{thm:pointwise_galois_realization}, suppose
\[
\Supp_R(H)=\Spec R.
\]
For every characteristic zero point \(x:R\to E'\) with \(\ker x\in U\subseteq\Spec R\), assume the coefficient topology and continuity hypotheses of \cref{thm:pointwise_galois_realization} and the declared classicality and Galois realization input. Then every such point is automorphic in the precise sense of \cref{thm:pointwise_galois_realization}.
\end{corollary}
records.proof_tex: Every point of \(U\) lies in the support, so \cref{thm:support_gives_hecke_system} gives a nonzero Hecke fiber. Apply the declared realization input and then \cref{thm:pointwise_galois_realization}.
records.normalized_claim: Full ordinary support gives pointwise automorphy on a locus for which all realization/topology/comparison inputs apply.
records.decisive_obligation: Locus only includes points satisfying named hypotheses

records.label: thm:derived_pointwise_realization
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Derived pointwise realization]\label{thm:derived_pointwise_realization}
Let \(e:R\cong\TT\), and let \(C\) be a perfect automorphic Hecke complex with full derived support. Choose a bounded finite projective model for \(C\), supported in degrees \([a,b]\). For every characteristic zero point \(x:R\to E'\), write \(y=x\circ e^{-1}\). Then some integer \(i\in[a,b]\) has
\[
H^i\left(C\mathbin{\mathop{\otimes}\limits_{\TT,y}^{\mathbf L}}E'\right)\neq0.
\]
Every \(t\in\TT\) acts on this cohomology through \(y(t)\).

For the realization conclusion, give \(E'\) a Hausdorff topological field structure. Supply a universal representation \(\rho_R\), a continuous specialization \(\rho_x=x\circ\rho_R\), and a semisimplification of \(\rho_x\). Suppose its characteristic polynomials on a Chebotarev dense set are \(y(P_v(X))\). Let the declared classicality range contain \([a,b]\). Assume that every nonzero Hecke eigensystem in that range is realized by a classical automorphic representation occurring in that degree, with a continuous semisimple attached representation whose characteristic polynomials on the same dense set are \(y(P_v(X))\). With the standard Chebotarev density and Brauer Nesbitt inputs of \cref{fact:chebotarev_brauer_nesbitt}, the specialization \(\rho_x\) is automorphic after semisimplification. If \(\rho_x\) is irreducible, it is itself isomorphic to the attached representation.
\end{theorem}
records.proof_tex:
Full derived support gives a nonzero fiber at \(y\). Scalar extension of the chosen projective model preserves its degree bounds. Its cohomology therefore vanishes below \(a\) and above \(b\). Since vanishing in every degree is equivalent to being zero in the derived category, some degree \(i\in[a,b]\) has nonzero cohomology. Choose a nonzero vector in that cohomology module.

Multiplication by \(t\in\TT\) is a cochain endomorphism of the original model. In the scalar extension the tensor relation identifies this endomorphism with \(y(t)\) times the identity. Passing to the derived category and then to cohomology preserves this equality. Thus the chosen vector is a common Hecke eigenvector with character \(y\).

The interval inclusion puts this eigensystem in the declared classicality range. Apply the realization input to obtain an occurring automorphic representation and its continuous semisimple attached representation. Its Frobenius characteristic polynomials agree with those of \(\rho_x\) on the prescribed dense set. Continuity extends the equality to every group element. The supplied semisimplification preserves these polynomials, so the general Brauer Nesbitt input gives an invertible linear intertwiner. If \(\rho_x\) is irreducible, it is already semisimple and the same comparison applies directly.
records.normalized_claim: Full derived Hecke support gives scalar nonzero cohomology in model interval; applicable classicality on that interval and comparison inputs give automorphy after semisimplification.
records.decisive_obligation: Surviving degree lies in classicality range; actual cohomology scalar action

records.label: thm:companion_branch_criterion
records.proof_tex: The disjoint union of the levels is an infinite rooted tree. It is locally finite because every level is finite. It contains a vertex at every depth. König's infinity lemma gives an infinite branch \cite{Diestel2017}. That branch is a point of the inverse limit.
records.normalized_claim: Finite nonempty levels and total reductions to fixed residual root admit a compatible branch.
records.decisive_obligation: Total maps, no transition-surjectivity assumption

records.label: cor:empty_companion_obstruction
records.proof_tex: A complete realization would reduce to a point at every finite level.
records.normalized_claim: An empty declared admissible finite level obstructs a complete realization reducing into all declared levels.
records.decisive_obligation: Admissibility coverage rather than arbitrary omitted realizations

records.label: thm:simultaneous_companion_completion
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Conditional simultaneous companion completion]\label{thm:simultaneous_companion_completion}
Under the coefficient and finite admissibility hypotheses above, one can choose continuous representations
\[
\rho_\lambda:\Gamma\longrightarrow\GL_D(\OO_\lambda)
\qquad(\lambda\in\Lambda)
\]
whose reduction class belongs to \(X_{\lambda,n}\) for every positive \(n\). They retain the declared residual class. After applying \(i_\lambda\), they are continuous, trivial on \(H_\lambda\), and satisfy
\[
\det\!\left(X- i_\lambda(\rho_\lambda(\gamma_v))\right)
=e_\lambda(P_v),\qquad v\in\Omega_\lambda.
\]
Their integral evaluation points factor through every actual quotient \(B_\lambda/J_{\lambda,u}\).
\end{theorem}
records.proof_tex:
The finitely generated ideal and finite residue ring give finite coefficient quotients at every precision. An individual conjugacy class has finitely many frames because the group of invertible basis matrices over each quotient is finite. Thus the finitely many admissible classes give a finite nonempty set of actual continuous representations at each positive level. Continuity is invariant under conjugation. Reduction gives total maps between these sets. Compactness, as in \cref{thm:companion_branch_criterion}, selects strictly compatible representatives. This step neither assumes transition surjectivity nor lifts a prescribed conjugating matrix.

Completeness and separatedness identify \(\GL_D(\OO_\lambda)\) with the compatible inverse limit of the quotient matrix groups. Lift entries and inverse entries to construct this identification. The two reduction and reconstruction identities hold entrywise. Finite quotient continuity implies continuity for the ideal adic topology, including the matrix inverse, so the reconstructed representation is continuous.

Each coefficient of its characteristic polynomial agrees with the prescribed integral coefficient modulo every positive power of \(I_\lambda\). Separatedness gives equality of the full polynomials. The same argument applied to the matrix entries of \(\rho_\lambda(g)-1\) gives triviality on \(H_\lambda\). Continuous coefficient change and the matching equations for \(P_{\lambda,v}\) give the asserted common spine over the local fields.

For \(p\in J_{\lambda,u}\), evaluation commutes with reduction. Its value is zero modulo every positive power of \(I_\lambda\), hence is zero integrally by separatedness. Therefore the evaluation homomorphism kills the whole ideal and factors uniquely through \(B_\lambda/J_{\lambda,u}\). Choose a realization for each \(\lambda\).
records.normalized_claim: Explicit finite occupied continuous class forests over complete separated finitely generated-adic coefficients give actual continuous integral representations with residual class, integral Frobenius/inertia relations and every-frame polynomial-ideal effectivity.
records.decisive_obligation: Compatible actual frames without conjugator lifts; continuity; integral polynomial data; every frame

records.label: thm:one_member_propagation
records.proof_tex: For every \(\lambda\), the two semisimple representations have the same unramified characteristic polynomials at all places outside one finite set. Apply \cref{fact:chebotarev_brauer_nesbitt}.
records.normalized_claim: Two existing semisimple compatible systems with same Frobenius spine, one linked to an automorphic object, agree at each coefficient place.
records.decisive_obligation: Both families exist and use same field/normalization/spine

records.label: prop:finite_frobenius_separator
records.proof_tex:
Let
\[
W
=
\operatorname{span}
\left\{
(t_1(\omega),\ldots,t_r(\omega)):\omega\in\Omega
\right\}
\subseteq E'^r.
\]
If \(W\neq E'^r\), a nonzero linear functional on \(E'^r\) would vanish on every evaluation vector, giving a nontrivial linear relation among the functions. Thus \(W=E'^r\). Choose \(r\) evaluation vectors forming a basis.
records.normalized_claim: r independent field-valued functions have r evaluation points with invertible matrix; known semisimple carrier multiplicities recovered when trace independence supplied.
records.decisive_obligation: Independence on full sample set; r=0; no arbitrary finite-prime classification

records.label: prop:dyadic_sign_projectors
records.statement_tex:
\begin{proposition}[Failure of integral sign projectors]\label{prop:dyadic_sign_projectors}
Let \(C_2=\langle g\rangle\). Over \(\QQ_2\), the two sign projectors are
\[
\boxed{
e_+=\frac{1+g}{2},
\qquad
e_-=\frac{1-g}{2}.
}
\]
Neither belongs to \(\ZZ_2[C_2]\). After reduction modulo two,
\[
\boxed{
\FF_2[C_2]
\cong
\FF_2[X]/(X^2),
\qquad
X=g-1.
}
\]
This ring is local and has no nontrivial idempotents.
\end{proposition}
records.proof_tex:
The displayed rational elements are the unique primitive idempotents because they project to the two characters of \(C_2\). Their coefficients contain \(1/2\), so they are not integral. In characteristic two,
\[
(g-1)^2=g^2-2g+1=0.
\]
The map \(X\mapsto g-1\) gives the displayed isomorphism. The quotient by \((X)\) is \(\FF_2\), and \((X)\) is nilpotent. Thus the ring is local.
records.normalized_claim: Unique two sign idempotents over Q2 are not integral in Z2[C2]; residual F2[C2] is dual numbers and local.
records.decisive_obligation: Coefficient denominators; actual residual quotient

records.label: cor:dyadic_coinvariant_recovery
records.proof_tex: Use the right module convention fixed in \cref{sec:auxiliary}. Quotienting by all balancing relations identifies \(M\otimes_{\Lambda,\epsilon}\OO\) with \(M/\fraka M\), without any commutativity assumption on \(\Delta\). Applying \(\epsilon\) to the coordinates of a finite \(\Lambda\) basis gives an \(\OO\) basis with the same index set.
records.normalized_claim: Finite free right module over any finite two-group algebra has free augmentation coinvariants of the same rank.
records.decisive_obligation: Nonabelian right-module convention; no character projectors

records.label: thm:ordinary_conditional_completion
records.proof_tex:
Full patched support descends to full support of \(H\) over \(R\) by
\cref{thm:ordinary_support_descent}. The isomorphism \(R\cong\TT\) transports that support by \cref{thm:rt_support_transport}. The field fiber is nonzero by
\cref{thm:support_gives_hecke_system}. The declared classicality and realization theorem supplies an automorphic representation in the fiber and an attached Galois representation. The comparison with \(\rho_x\) follows from \cref{thm:pointwise_galois_realization}.
records.normalized_claim: Actual ordinary completion datum, full patched support, comparison, and all explicit pointwise inputs give nonzero fiber and classical automorphic realization after semisimplification.
records.decisive_obligation: Universal-specialization polynomial match explicitly supplied; topology/continuity retained

records.label: thm:derived_conditional_completion
records.proof_tex:
Full support descends from the patched perfect complex by \cref{thm:derived_support_descent}. Scalar transport through \(e\), followed by the actual derived isomorphism with the automorphic Hecke complex, gives full support for \(C\). Its fiber at \(y\) is therefore nonzero. The bounded model and induced Hecke action argument in \cref{thm:derived_pointwise_realization} supplies a nonzero cohomology eigenvector in an integer degree within the model's bounds.

If realization applies to this eigensystem, it supplies the occurring automorphic object and a continuous semisimple attached representation with the declared Frobenius polynomials. The representation comparison in \cref{thm:derived_pointwise_realization} then identifies the supplied semisimplification of \(\rho_x\) with that attached representation. Only applicability to this eigensystem is used; a classicality theorem for every degree in a prescribed interval is unnecessary.
records.normalized_claim: Actual derived completion datum gives nonzero scalar cohomological eigensystem; realization applicable to that selected eigensystem gives automorphy after semisimplification.
records.decisive_obligation: No uniform classicality in irrelevant degrees; same polynomial/density inputs

records.label: thm:system_completion
records.proof_tex: The completion theorem at \(\lambda_0\) gives the automorphic representation \(\pi\). Apply \cref{thm:one_member_propagation} to the two compatible systems.
records.normalized_claim: An already identified automorphic member and an existing same-spine attached family identify an existing semisimple system memberwise.
records.decisive_obligation: Same automorphic object; same algebraic spine; no member construction

records.label: thm:five_gate_completion
records.statement_tex:
\begin{theorem}[Five gate formulation]\label{thm:five_gate_completion}
Fix a characteristic zero deformation point \(x:R\to E'\). Give \(E'\) a Hausdorff topological field structure. The conditional argument uses the following five gates.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Residual gate.} Residual occupancy in the declared automorphic carrier and representability of the chosen deformation problem are supplied arithmetic inputs. In particular, the deformation ring \(R\) and its universal representation \(\rho_R\) are available.
\item \textbf{Patching gate.} An applicable patching theorem supplies an ordinary finite module or a perfect complex with full patched support, together with the coefficient quotient and the module or derived control isomorphism. Write \(M\) for the resulting finite level carrier over \(R\).
\item \textbf{Comparison gate.} Let \(H\) be a finite ordinary Hecke module or a perfect Hecke complex over \(\TT\). Supply a ring map \(f:R\to\TT\) satisfying
\[
(f^*)^{-1}\bigl(\Supp_R(M)\bigr)\subseteq\Supp_{\TT}(H).
\]
Use ordinary or derived support according to the carrier. Actual scalar extension satisfies this inclusion, as does transport through a ring isomorphism with the corresponding carrier identification.
\item \textbf{Fiber gate.} Supply a Hecke point \(y:\TT\to E'\) with \(y\circ f=x\). Then the fiber of \(H\) at \(y\) is nonzero. It contains a nonzero Hecke eigenvector, in some integer cohomological degree in the derived case, with character \(y\).
\item \textbf{Realization gate.} The declared classicality theorem applies to the resulting eigensystem and supplies an occurring classical automorphic representation \(\pi\), with a continuous semisimple attached representation. Require the specialization \(\rho_x=x\circ\rho_R\) to be continuous and supply its semisimplification. On the same Chebotarev dense set, assume that the characteristic polynomials of both \(\rho_x\) and the attached representation are \(y(P_v(X))\). Retain the standard density and general Brauer Nesbitt inputs of \cref{fact:chebotarev_brauer_nesbitt}.
\end{enumerate}
Then \(\rho_x^{\mathrm{ss}}\) is isomorphic to the representation attached to \(\pi\). If \(\rho_x\) is irreducible, the same conclusion holds for \(\rho_x\) itself.

For propagation, suppose both a semisimple compatible family \(\{\rho_\lambda\}\) containing \(\rho_x\) and a family \(\{\rho_{\pi,\lambda}\}\) attached to this same \(\pi\) already exist. Require the distinguished members to be \(\rho_x\) and its attached representation, respectively. Assume the coefficient, continuity, density, semisimplification and common algebraic Frobenius spine hypotheses of \cref{thm:one_member_propagation}, with that spine agreeing with the specialized Hecke polynomials at the distinguished place. Then
\[
\rho_\lambda\cong\rho_{\pi,\lambda}^{\mathrm{ss}}
\qquad\text{for every }\lambda.
\]
\end{theorem}
records.proof_tex:
The residual and representability inputs specify the setting in which the supplied patching theorem applies. The formal deduction begins with its actual rings, carriers and comparison maps. In the ordinary branch, finite generation and full support at finite level follow from the coefficient quotient and module control isomorphism. In the derived branch, the derived control isomorphism gives a perfect finite level model, and \cref{thm:derived_support_descent} gives full support.

The comparison inclusion transports this full support to \(H\). More specifically, \(y\circ f=x\) identifies the contraction of \(\ker y\) with \(\ker x\), so support at the source point gives support at the Hecke point. In the ordinary case, \cref{thm:field_fiber_criterion} gives a nonzero actual tensor fiber. In the derived case, the support criterion gives a nonzero actual derived fiber and hence a nonzero cohomology vector. Its integer degree lies within the bounds of the chosen finite projective model. In both cases, multiplication on the original carrier induces the scalar \(y(t)\) on the specialized vector for every \(t\in\TT\).

Choose this nonzero eigensystem and apply the declared realization theorem to it. No realization statement in other degrees is needed. The two continuous representations have the same characteristic polynomials on the declared dense Frobenius conjugacy classes. Continuity extends their equality to the whole group. The supplied semisimplification preserves those polynomials, and the general Brauer Nesbitt input gives the required invertible linear intertwiner. The irreducible conclusion follows as in \cref{thm:pointwise_galois_realization}.

Finally, retain the same \(\pi\) in its attached family. The distinguished member identities connect both families to the pointwise construction, while the common algebraic spine gives the required Frobenius polynomials at every coefficient place. Apply \cref{thm:one_member_propagation} to these two existing families. The construction does not produce a missing companion or an attached compatible family.
